Measured at 1280 on all 13 cards: when the sheet appears, the clicked card's bottom edge is between -29px and -1029px, i.e. ABOVE the top of the viewport, every single time. The sheet is a sibling AFTER the whole 1,429px wall, so clicking a card in row 1 scrolls you past four rows of other cards. The owner asked to 'click through that and see what was discussed' - the card and its detail have to stay together.

FINDING 2 - level 2 is the log dump, one click down instead of zero. Sheet heights at 1280 run 1,146 to 8,038px (median 2,825). 'Decision browsing', with three serving tasks, is 8,038px - nine screens - because each task section renders that task's entire landing report plus every log line. The owner: 'a lot of that decision-making process, I don't want to see it right away. We tend to get into too much detail too early.'

FINDING 3 - four images in level 2 are broken. A serving task's outcome is written to be read on its own page, so its image paths are relative (picker.jpg, chip.jpg, browse-1920.jpg, color-1280.jpg). Rendered inside the run's page they resolve against the RUN's url and 404. Confirmed by watching the network: 4 distinct 404s on opening three sheets.

FINDING 4 - not one card is a preview: 13 of 13 are text only. picture() reads only ext/JSONL's `shot` verb, and no serving task logged one (0 shot lines across 7 task.jsonl files) - yet six of the seven embed a screenshot in their outcome markdown. The owner asked for the asks 'listed as previews, when possible'.

FINDING 5 - one card carries two pills that go to the same place. 'Session as chat' shows both 'the prompt' and 'the prompt, in the ...' pointing at the identical url. Across the wall that url is linked 14 times under 2 labels.

FINDING 6 - a deliverable pill can be a clipped sentence. 'The layout browser ...', 'The lab - today's r...', 'the task (skill sec...' - a 20-character clip of a sentence-length label names nothing the reader can act on.

FINDING 7 - the prompts rail is a single 26px row and never says what it is. On this run's session there is exactly 1 owner message (the transcript holds 447 lines, 86 top-level user lines, 8 with text, 7 of which are task-notifications the trivial() filter correctly drops). So at 1920 a lone clipped copy of the message sits in a 240px column beside the 960px stream that holds the same sentence - a control whose click has no visible consequence.

FINDING 8 - on a real conversation the rail is a wall of identical rows. 2026-09-13/page-cms: 64 rail items, of which 16 of the first 20 read '/mastermind'. A table of contents whose rows cannot be told apart is not one.
FINDING 9 - an unrecognised tool leaks its raw camelCase name into the run label: 'thought, loaded 2 skills, ran 22 commands, edited 10 files, spawned 6 agents, ScheduleWakeup'.
FINDING 10 - the wall's head is a count, not a statement of what the tab is: '13 ASKS'. A stranger cannot say in ten seconds what they are looking at.
FINDING 11 - nothing on a card says the card opens. The only affordance is cursor:pointer and a hover outline, neither of which exists in a still screenshot or on a touch screen.

FIXED 1 - the sheet is now a member of the wall grid (grid-column 1 / -1) and row_end() slots it after the last card sharing the clicked card's offsetTop. FIXED 8 - every rail row carries its time, so a mastermind session's rail is a timeline instead of a wall of duplicates: 2026-09-13/page-cms went from 16 identical '/mastermind' rows in the first 20 to 64 of 64 distinct, and its list still scrolls (2,005 over 739px). assign.outcome:
**Found 13, fixed 13, left 2.** Every control on the Asks tab and the Session tab, pressed headless at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440, against your own sentences.

**The two that mattered.** Clicking a card used to drop you a screen below it — measured on all 13 cards, the card you clicked was between 29 and 1,029px *above* the top of the screen by the time its detail appeared. The sheet now opens inside the wall, directly under that card's row, and the card stays put. And level 2 was the log dump you asked not to see: the three-task sheet was 8,038px, nine screens. It is now the quote, then per task one headline, its links and the lines where something was decided — 2,131px at its worst, 991 in the middle — with the full report one more fold down.

**And the wall is a wall of previews now.** Not one of the 13 cards had a picture: the code only read logged `shot` lines and no task had logged one, while six of seven had a screenshot sitting in their landing report. Eleven of thirteen cards show one.

![The sheet opens under the card you clicked, and the cards carry pictures](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/asks-critic/after-1280.jpg)

**The other ten.** Four broken images in the sheet, from links a task wrote relative to its own directory (0 failed requests now; 165 links across ten pages, none still relative) · a card pill that navigated to a 404 · two pills on one card going to the same place · pill labels that were clipped sentences ("The layout browser — t…" → "The layout browser") · an outcome headline printing its own markdown source · the prompts rail, which was one clipped copy of the message beside it and never said what it was — hidden below two prompts, named above two · a rail of 16 identical `/mastermind` rows on a real session — every row carries its time, 64 of 64 distinct now · `ScheduleWakeup` leaking raw into a run label · a head reading "13 ASKS" · and no cue at all that a card opens.

**Left, both outside the fence.** `minion-skill` logged its three deliverables as repo paths under `.claude/`, which are not places a browser can go — the card refuses them, but the data is a landed task's. At 360 the fourth tab sits past the edge; the bar swipes, and `ext/tabs` owns it.
